Hi Jonas —

Thanks for the proposal this morning. We had a quick sync with finance and procurement and they asked for a clearer timeline on the uplift, and whether the soft-throttle will start immediately or after the PO is processed. We also need a one-page summary for our procurement team that aligns monthly commit (tokens) to invoice cadence.

Key constraints on our side:
- Preferred effective date: 2026-07-01 to align with our July cycle.
- We need a 2-week canary (limited routes) before full rollout.
- Billing must show a prorated charge for July if the PO clears mid-month.

Could you confirm the above and send the one-pager? Also, Marco will be the central contact for the PO.

Thanks,
Amy
VP, Engineering 
Ivy Retail

> Amy — thanks again for taking the call. Attached is a working MAP and proposed step-up. I sketched a staged rollout so you get a canary window + automatic soft-throttle protection if we hit the committed bandwidth ceiling.

> - New monthly commit: 1.2B tokens (up from 600M) starting 2026-07-01.
> - 2-week canary (select routes) 2026-07-01 — 2026-07-14.
> - Full route migration 2026-07-15 with automatic fallback to 600M variant if soft-throttle triggers.
> - Prorated July billing for the uplift window.
>

> — Jonas

Ben / Laura —

Looping you in. Procurement asked for the one-pager and confirmation on the effective date. Amy prefers 2026-07-01 and wants a two-week canary. Questions for ops/legal/finance:

1) Can we guarantee a prorated invoice calculation and include the prorate line item in the DocuSign? (Finance)
2) Is the soft-throttle behavior described below acceptable for a customer-facing SLA note? (Ben, you and I discussed a "soft-throttle" that delays non-critical low-priority background requests — I want to make sure wording is consistent.)
3) Ops: confirm we can configure the canary by route and the automatic fallback trigger (e.g., 95% of committed throughput sustained for >5 minutes).

I attached the MAP draft. I'll produce the one-page procurement summary and the DocuSign draft once we confirm answers.

Thanks —
Jonas

> Attachment: Ivy_Mutual_Action_Plan_v2.pdf
From: ben_carter@redwood.ai
To: jonas_weber@redwood.ai, laura_bennett@redwood.ai
Date: Mon, 21 Jun 2026 12:42:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: FW: Hosted API commit uplift — staged rollout & rate smoothing

Jonas —

Finance can do prorated billing; we already support mid-month commit changes with a line item that shows the daily pro rata uplift. I'll get a sample invoice line to include in the one-pager.

On the soft-throttle language: suggest we say "graceful degradation to priority routing" and specify observable triggers (e.g., sustained 95% usage for 5m OR spike above 120% instantaneous for >30s). That lets us be firm without promising hard guarantees. Also recommend we include a rollback policy: automatic fallback to the 600M variant if we see >2% error-rate increase sustained for 10m during canary.

Ops note (Laura) — can you confirm the fallback trigger thresholds and whether route-scoped canary is doable?

— Ben
Account Executive
From: laura_bennett@redwood.ai
To: ben_carter@redwood.ai, jonas_weber@redwood.ai, amy@ivyretail.com
Date: Tue, 22 Jun 2026 09:30:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: FW: Hosted API commit uplift — staged rollout & rate smoothing

Amy / Team —

Confirming ops can run a route-scoped canary. Proposed operational plan:
- 2026-07-01 00:00 — enable canary on 10% of traffic (checkout, recommendations routes only).
- Monitoring: token throughput, p50/p95 latency, error-rate, and model-quality drift (existing eval hooks).
- Fallback triggers: sustained 95% committed throughput for 5m OR error-rate +2% sustained 10m => immediate rollback to 600M variant + alert to both teams.
- Full rollout 2026-07-15 if canary passes 72h stability window.

I'll work with our SRE on runbooks and will share a one-page procurement summary before EOD Wednesday. We'll include the prorated invoice example Ben mentioned and a DocuSign link.

Laura Bennett
Senior Customer Ops
Redwood Inference
